tips.title: Dry Fitting Tip: Use a Caliper to Measure Part Clearances
tips.text: When dry fitting parts, use a digital caliper to measure the clearances between mating surfaces. This ensures that parts will fit together as intended without the need for sanding or filing, which can weaken the material.

tips.title: Structural Support Tip: Use Torsion Rods for Stronger Support
tips.text: When building scale models, use torsion rods instead of traditional metal rods for structural support. Torsion rods distribute force more evenly and are less prone to bending, making them ideal for supporting heavy or complex structures.

tips.title: Modifying Parts Tip: Use a Dremel with a Carbide Bit for Accurate Cutting
tips.text: When modifying scale model parts, use a Dremel rotary tool equipped with a carbide cutting bit. The carbide bit provides a high degree of accuracy and can cut through materials like plastic and resin without generating excessive heat or vibration.

tips.title: Seam Filling Tip: Use a Flexible Polyurethane Sealant for Smooth Finishing
tips.text: When filling seams in scale models, use a flexible polyurethane sealant. This type of sealant dries hard but remains flexible, allowing it to absorb minor stresses and movements without cracking or breaking, providing a smooth and durable finish.

tips.title: Construction Sequencing Tip: Build from the Center Outwards to Maintain Structural Integrity
tips.text: When building scale models, it's essential to construct from the center outwards. This approach ensures that the structure remains stable and prevents it from becoming too top-heavy or unstable, maintaining the integrity of the model throughout the assembly process.
